I think one of the worst cases for me in CS:GO is the hit reg for the CT's in Dust 2. Sometimes I got my sights directly on their heads and shoot, but it doesn't hit them. I've had my sights directly on his head and he wasn't moving, but when I fired, it didn't hit. The game has some problems, no doubt.

An important thing to know is that the bullet holes on the wall mean nothing. They don't accurately reflect where the bullets go as far as what the server sees.

Basically, there are 4 recoil/spread mechanics going on, 3 of which are controllable. When you move, you get a ton of movement inaccuracy, so really do your best to not move. Play deathmatch and try to get in adad battles, and shoot exactly when you stop moving. The second controllable mechanic is the spray pattern, which is unique to each gun and always the exact same (though it shrinks a little when you crouch). You can learn to draw the mirror of the recoil pattern so that your bullets all go to generally the same place (note that the bullets start going to a different place relative to your crosshair, AND your crosshair bounces). The controllable mechanic is reset: when you fire or move it takes a little while for the gun to get back to its most accurate, and this time depends on the gun.

There is also some cone spread on each bullet which is unique to the gun and independent of the other spread mechanics. For example, from pit to barrels on dust 2, you basically can't reliably hit a headshot with an AK. At that distance the AK isn't accurate enough to reliably get a headshot, even with perfect aim.

Back on the meaningless bullet holes thing: the randomized spread mechanics are calculated twice, client side and server side. Only the server side calculation matters for hit detection, client side is just for visual effects. You can just ignore bullet holes and bullet tracers.
